name: Half Marathon — Intermediate

workouts.name: 40min Fartlek
workouts.description: Unstructured speed play — alternate between hard surges and easy running by feel.
workouts.notes: Unstructured surges to open the block — let effort, not the watch, set the hard 2-min pushes. Recoveries should feel like a genuine reset before the next surge, not a jog-through.

workouts.name: 5km Tempo Run
workouts.description: Sustained threshold-pace effort. Develops lactate clearance and mental focus.
workouts.notes: Controlled-uncomfortable, not a race. You should be able to speak in broken sentences, not full ones — settle into that effort by the second kilometre and hold it flat.

workouts.name: 9km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.
workouts.notes: Fully conversational the whole way — this is aerobic economy and time-on-feet, not a fitness test. If you're breathing hard you're going too fast; slow down.

workouts.name: 9km Recovery Run
workouts.description: Very easy effort to promote blood flow and recovery. Keep the pace comfortable.
workouts.notes: Swapped from hill reps: your HRV read 'Unbalanced' this morning and readiness is soft (44) on top of a recent anaerobic-heavy stretch. Hills wait until you've absorbed that load — keep this fully easy, the goal is blood flow, not stimulus.

workouts.name: 8km Progressive Run
workouts.description: Start easy, finish fast. Each third gets progressively faster developing pacing discipline.
workouts.notes: Three even thirds building from easy to threshold — a smooth ladder, not a jump. Hold each third honestly and don't rush into the fast finish; let the pace climb on its own.

workouts.name: 10km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.
workouts.notes: Steady and easy — check in on how the legs feel after yesterday's swap. This should feel comfortably repeatable, the kind of run you could describe as 'pleasant' afterwards.

workouts.name: 8km Easy + 6 Strides
workouts.description: Easy run finishing with short strides to develop running economy and neuromuscular coordination.
workouts.notes: Easy running with 6 short strides at the end — relaxed and fast, not a sprint. Think 'smooth acceleration,' cue tall posture and quick turnover, then walk back fully recovered.

workouts.name: 6km Tempo Run
workouts.description: Sustained threshold-pace effort. Develops lactate clearance and mental focus.
workouts.notes: Your longest tempo block yet — 6km at threshold. Go out slightly conservative through the first 2km; the goal is an even effort you can hold to the last stride, not a fade.

workouts.name: 10km Progressive Long Run
workouts.description: Start easy, build to marathon pace, finish at threshold. Develops pacing and fatigue resistance.
workouts.notes: Start easy, ease into marathon effort, finish the last tenth at threshold. Mental-toughness work — the finish should feel purposeful, not desperate. Bank the pacing discipline for race day.

workouts.name: 30min Fartlek
workouts.description: Unstructured speed play — alternate between hard surges and easy running by feel.
workouts.notes: Cutback week — shorter fartlek, same crisp surges. This is about absorbing the last three weeks, not adding more load. Keep the hard bits genuinely hard and brief.

workouts.name: 8km Progressive Run
workouts.description: Start easy, finish fast. Each third gets progressively faster developing pacing discipline.
workouts.notes: A shorter version of the ladder — easy, marathon, threshold. Light legs, clean form. Use it to check that recent fatigue is clearing, not to chase a number.

workouts.name: 8km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.
workouts.notes: Deliberately shorter long run this week. Easy pace throughout — this is recovery volume banked for the build phase ahead, not a session to push.

workouts.name: 6 x 3.0min VO2max Intervals
workouts.description: Hard intervals at VO2max intensity to raise aerobic ceiling. Full recovery between reps.
workouts.notes: Hard reps at I-pace with full jog recovery between — sharper than the fartlek surges. Effort should be 'hard but repeatable' on rep 1 through rep 6: even splits, not a fast start that fades.

workouts.name: 4km Tempo Run
workouts.description: Sustained threshold-pace effort. Develops lactate clearance and mental focus.
workouts.notes: Threshold effort — settle in by kilometre two and hold it, 'comfortably hard,' the pace you could sustain for about an hour if you had to.

workouts.name: 10km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.
workouts.notes: Easy aerobic long run — first big-block long run of the build. Relaxed effort; save the legs for Thursday's intervals next week.

workouts.name: 11 x 400m Speed Reps
workouts.description: Short, fast repetitions developing speed and running economy at R pace.
workouts.notes: Fast 400s at R-pace with a full jog recovery — this is neuromuscular speed and form, not a lactate session. Relaxed arms, quick turnover, and stop a rep early if form breaks down.

workouts.name: 5 x 5min Cruise Intervals
workouts.description: Broken threshold work with short recoveries. Same lactate benefit as tempo with less mental fatigue.
workouts.notes: Broken threshold — same lactate-clearance benefit as a tempo run with less mental grind thanks to the short jog recoveries. Hold each 5-min rep dead even; don't let the first one be the fastest.

workouts.name: 11km Progressive Long Run
workouts.description: Start easy, build to marathon pace, finish at threshold. Develops pacing and fatigue resistance.
workouts.notes: Building block — easy into marathon effort into threshold to close. Practice staying relaxed as the pace rises; tension in the shoulders is the first sign you're overreaching.

workouts.name: 12 x 45s Hill Reps
workouts.description: Hill repetitions build strength, power, and running economy. Effort should be hard but controlled.
workouts.notes: Shorter, punchier hill reps than week 2's — power and running economy. Drive the arms and knees on the way up, then float back down easy; the recovery jog is part of the session.

workouts.name: 10km Progressive Run
workouts.description: Start easy, finish fast. Each third gets progressively faster developing pacing discipline.
workouts.notes: Easy, marathon, threshold thirds — a rehearsal for controlling effort as fatigue builds, which is exactly what race day asks of you.

workouts.name: 10km Long Run w/ 3km Race Pace
workouts.description: Long run with a sustained race-pace block to build specificity and confidence.
workouts.notes: First taste of goal race effort inside a long run — settle into the 3km block only once you're warm, and resist the urge to push it faster than that effort.

workouts.name: 32min Fartlek
workouts.description: Unstructured speed play — alternate between hard surges and easy running by feel.
workouts.notes: Cutback week — same fartlek shape as week 4, a touch longer. Trust the taper-down; the fitness from the last three weeks needs this week to actually stick.

workouts.name: 4 x 1.2km Race Pace Intervals
workouts.description: Race-specific intervals at marathon pace. Builds confidence and specificity.
workouts.notes: A shorter, easier version of the race-pace intervals to come — 4 x 1.2km at goal effort with a jog rest. Smooth and even, not a test.

workouts.name: 8km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.
workouts.notes: Easy, shorter long run to close the cutback. Full recovery effort — the legs should feel fresher by Sunday evening than they did Friday.

workouts.name: 7 x 2.5min VO2max Intervals
workouts.description: Hard intervals at VO2max intensity to raise aerobic ceiling. Full recovery between reps.
workouts.notes: More, shorter reps than week 5's — quicker turnover at the same I-pace. These should feel sharp, almost fast-feeling by the last two reps once you're warmed into it.

workouts.name: 5 x 6min Cruise Intervals
workouts.description: Broken threshold work with short recoveries. Same lactate benefit as tempo with less mental fatigue.
workouts.notes: Longer reps than week 6's cruise intervals — 6-minute blocks that ask for patience. Same threshold effort, just a longer time to hold your composure inside each rep.

workouts.name: 12km Progressive Long Run
workouts.description: Start easy, build to marathon pace, finish at threshold. Develops pacing and fatigue resistance.
workouts.notes: Peak-phase progressive long run — the biggest one yet. Be patient through the easy portion; the marathon- and threshold-pace finish will feel earned, not forced, if you are.

workouts.name: 16 x 400m Speed Reps
workouts.description: Short, fast repetitions developing speed and running economy at R pace.
workouts.notes: More reps than week 6's — same sharp 400s at R-pace, deeper into the session. Quality over the first 10 matters more than gutting out the last 6; drop a rep if form goes.

workouts.name: 5 x 1.4km Race Pace Intervals
workouts.description: Race-specific intervals at marathon pace. Builds confidence and specificity.
workouts.notes: Longer race-pace blocks than week 8's — 1.4km at goal effort. This is the closest rehearsal yet to holding half-marathon effort for real; even splits across all five reps is the win.

workouts.name: 11km Long Run w/ 4km Race Pace
workouts.description: Long run with a sustained race-pace block to build specificity and confidence.
workouts.notes: The peak long run — a 4km race-effort block inside it, longer than week 7's. Treat that block like the middle of the actual race: locked in, not laboured.

workouts.name: 7km Easy + 6 Strides
workouts.description: Easy run finishing with short strides to develop running economy and neuromuscular coordination.
workouts.notes: Easy running with a handful of relaxed strides to keep the legs sharp as volume drops. Effort stays low — this is about feeling fast for a few seconds, not training.

workouts.name: 4km Tempo Run
workouts.description: Sustained threshold-pace effort. Develops lactate clearance and mental focus.
workouts.notes: Short, crisp reminder of threshold effort — shorter than week 3's or week 5's tempo. Legs should feel noticeably fresher than they did mid-block.

workouts.name: 8km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.
workouts.notes: Easy taper long run — comfortably under peak distance. The fitness is banked; this is about staying loose, not building anything new.

workouts.name: Easy shakeout
workouts.description: Easy shakeout
workouts.notes: Easy shakeout, nothing more. Effort should feel almost too easy — that's the point with the race five days out.

workouts.name: Short shakeout with strides
workouts.description: Short shakeout with strides
workouts.notes: Short and easy with a few strides to wake the legs up. Resist any urge to test race pace this close to the start.

workouts.name: RACE DAY — Half Marathon
workouts.description: RACE DAY — Half Marathon
workouts.notes: Race day. Trust the training — start controlled through the first 5km, settle into goal effort, and save something for the last 3km. You've done the work.
